newsitem.title: UK: Mark on hold as market eyes Italy rate situation.
newsitem.headline: Mark on hold as market eyes Italy rate situation.

text.p: The mark was on hold against the lira in morning Europe as the market zoomed in on Italy amid optimism that it would be able to join EMU from the outset and renewed expectations of an Italian rate cut in the near future.

Sparking speculation of lower rates was Italy's latest repurchase tender, in which the Bank of Italy set the minimum rate for the repo at 6.26 percent compared to the 6.90 percent at the previous tender on Tuesday.

"People are not quite sure what to make of it, and are keeping an eye out for a rate move later today," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered, adding that the Bank of Italy usually waited until the markets closed before it made any interest rate moves.

The market attached particular significance to the repo, coming as it did on the heels of Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi's comment on Tuesday that he expected rates to fall as the markets became convinced of the structural nature of Italy's lower inflation and healthier public accounts.
Ciampi said on Wednesday that the stability and strength of the lira raised expectations of a fall in short-term rates.
Traders, however, said they were wary of making any big moves now.

"The lira's had a good run against the mark recently...There's been a lot of news out about Italy, and it looks like people want to keep things on hold for now," said one trader at a Japanese bank in London.
The lira was at 977.55/85 to the mark at 1025 GMT, slightly weaker than 977.15/30 seen in late European trade on Tuesday. It hit a four-month high of 976.00 lire in overnight trade.
However, there was some wariness about assuming that the repo rate signalled an imminent rate cut.

"It can be seen as a sign that the Bank of Italy is biased towards lower interest rates, but it doesn't necessarily signal that there will be a discount rate cut," said Ernesto Ramirez, European economist at Bankers Trust.
The Italian discount rate is at 6.75 percent, almost half a point above Wednesday's repo rate.
Italian bonds rocketed on the rate cut speculation, with the spread between 10-year Italian BTPs and bunds falling to a record low of 115 basis points.
Ciampi added fuel to the rally by saying the BTP/bund spread can still fall further.

Even before Wednesday's renewed rate cut speculation, BTPs had been rallying in recent days on increasing expectations that Italy would be able to join Europe's monetary union from the outset in 1999 and further signs of falling inflation.
Some analysts said today's repo rate could be natural under such circumstances.

"If you take a rational view of the repo tender, you could say it was more a reflection of the market conditions rather than a signal from the Bank of Italy," said Ken Wattret, economist at Banque Paribas.

Wattret said caution was needed over assuming an imminent rate cut, pointing out that if Italy had intended to cut interest rates on the basis of conditions like low inflation and unemployment, it would have done so already.
Preliminary Italian inflation from 11 sample cities published in recent days ponted to an inflation rate of 1.4-1.5 percent for June, down from 1.6 in May.
Meanwhile, Italy's jobless rate rose to 12.5 percent in April from 12.4 percent in January, according to data issued on Wednesday.
Analysts said the Bank of Italy could well wait until the national budget situation became clearer in the autumn before making a move on interest rates.
-- Chizu Nomiyama, London Forex Desk, +44-171-542-6721
